title: The arch in the sky
text: A rainbow is not an object but a {{1}}: every observer sees a different one, assembled from different raindrops, and nobody has ever reached the end of one. The optics are strict. Sunlight enters a raindrop, {{2}} once inside, and leaves split into colours — red bent least, violet most. Because the geometry is fixed, the bow always {{3}} at the same angle from the point exactly opposite the sun, which is why you can never approach it: move, and the bow moves with you. From an aeroplane, with no horizon to {{4}} the circle, rainbows appear complete — a fact that still startles first-time fliers. Double bows {{5}} from a second reflection inside the drop, and the second bow's colours {{6}} their order, a detail painters get wrong surprisingly often. The dark band between the two — Alexander's band — is real: raindrops there {{7}} no light towards you at all. For a phenomenon {{8}} in myth as a promise and a bridge, the rainbow is impressively indifferent to us: it is simply what sunlight does to rain, at exactly forty-two degrees.

gaps.explanation: 'not an object but an effect' — a visual result; defect = a fault, reflect = bounce back.
'reflects once inside' — bounces off the back of the drop; refrain takes 'from', relapse = fall back into illness.
'the bow always hangs at the same angle' — stays suspended there; hanker takes 'after'.
'no horizon to block the circle' — obstruct the view of it; bolster = support and strengthen.
'double bows result from a second reflection' — 'result from' = arise from; consult = seek advice.
'the second bow's colours invert their order' — turn them upside down, red outermost becoming innermost; incite = stir up.
'raindrops there send no light towards you' — direct none your way; the geometry sends light elsewhere, which is why the band is dark.
'a phenomenon cast in myth as a promise' — assigned a part, like an actor is cast; court = seek the favour of.
